author: zanor
quote:
Waiting over a decade only to get a choppy 30 FPS life sim on the PS5 is a massive letdown.
Instead of the fast paced, chaotic crime sandbox that made the series legendary, Rockstar delivered a slow relationship simulator weighed down by tedious realism. Between babysitting character meters, rigid mission design, and endless mundane chores, the game feels like it actively gets in the way of having actual fun. You spend far more time managing life sim mechanics and sitting through sluggish animations than causing mayhem.
The technical state on PS5 is just as disappointing. Fast driving and shootouts feel unresponsive with constant frame rate drops, and the launch is packed with serious bugs. Players are falling straight through the map in the opening minutes, hitting mission softlocks where cutscenes fail to trigger, and dealing with broken physics where cars launch into the air and NPCs clip through objects. On top of that, frequent CE-108255-1 crash errors, lost save progress, and overheating issues that force the PS5 to shut down make it tough to even play.
Great visuals and a massive map mean nothing when the core gameplay feels like a glitchy chore list running in slow motion. Rockstar lost sight of what made Grand Theft Auto fun in the first place, and it simply does not live up to the hype or the price tag.
